findings:
🟠 [verdict-not-rederived] MUST-FIX In scripts/check-phase-review-receipt.js, the `review` branch trusts `receipt.verdict` directly (the only check is `if (receipt.verdict !== 'SHIP-AS-IS') process.exit(1)`) and never re-derives the verdict from the underlying artifacts. An implementer can hand-write `receipt-<phase>.json` with `verdict: "SHIP-AS-IS"`, a fabricated `review-<phase>/chain.json` whose every entry's `base`/`head` is consistent with `phase_base_sha`, and matching `review-<phase>/g<n>/range.json` files whose `diff_sha256` is recomputed trivially by running the same `git diff A B` command — every existing gate check (chain contiguity, range.json base/head equality, diff_sha256 recomputation, last chain head == current branch head) then passes and the gate exits 0, even though no `dispatch-review.sh` ever ran and no `findings.json` exists. This violates ADR-0001 ("verdicts are re-derived from artifacts, never trusted from a claim") and is exactly the "can an implementer forge a passing receipt?" failure mode the spec asks the reviewer to detect. Smallest remediation: after the existing chain/range/diff_sha256 checks pass, iterate every finalized chain entry, read `<ledger>/review-<phase>/g<n>/findings.json` and the file at that entry's `dispositions_path` (per the schema `finalize` writes into chain), recompute `hasVerifiedCritical` and `openFindings`, and require `receipt.verdict` to equal `'FIX-THEN-SHIP'` iff any Critical finding has `disposition==='verified'`; also require that each `g<n>/findings.json` actually exists. Exit 1 on any mismatch. Add a test case that hand-crafts a `receipt-*.json` with `verdict:"SHIP-AS-IS"` while the linked findings.json contains a Critical finding with disposition=verified and assert exit 1.
🔵 [chain-json-append-race] CUT/FOLLOW-UP hetero-review-loop.js `handleCollect` reads then appends to `chain.json` with no file lock or atomic rename; two concurrent collects on the same phase could lose an entry. Excluded from this version: callers serialize by generation in current flow; no test exercises concurrent collect on the same phase, and the worst observed effect is a self-recovering retry rather than a forged gate pass.
🔵 [opt-out-empty-config-pass] CUT/FOLLOW-UP check-phase-review-receipt.js opt-out branch computes `sha256(Buffer.alloc(0))` when `config_source.path` does not exist and compares against `receipt.config_source.sha256`. A receipt claiming `config_source.sha256 == e3b0c44...` (sha256 of empty) for a non-existent path therefore passes alongside a resolver stub returning `off`. Excluded: opt-out is gated by the resolver's current `off` value (the actual knob truth per ADR-0001); the config-source sha is informational metadata, and the resolver stub is the security boundary. No spec line requires stricter config-source validation.
🔵 [closed-findings-by-absence] CUT/FOLLOW-UP `handleFinalize` marks an earlier-generation verified finding `closed_by_generation: N` whenever it is absent from generation N's `findings.json`, even if the absence is unrelated to the prior finding's fix (reviewer may simply have missed it). Excluded: the spec defines closure as absence-in-later-findings; this matches the intended semantic and any tightening belongs to a future review-policy deliverable.
🔵 [resolver-empty-repoRoot-modeA-optout] CUT/FOLLOW-UP check-phase-review-receipt.js opt-out branch passes `''` to `runResolverField` when `--repo-root` is absent, while Mode A review branch uses `process.cwd()` for git ops. Inconsistent but unreachable in practice because the test suite always passes `--repo-root`. Excluded: cosmetic; would surface as a self-failing test if it ever bit.
